name: Should you remove a pool before selling a house?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to remove an old in-ground pool before listing a home for sale?
mainEntity.text: Is it better to remove an old in-ground pool before listing a home for sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether to remove a pool before selling depends on what local buyers expect and how the property will present afterward. If the pool is old, damaged, expensive to maintain, or takes up space buyers would rather use for landscaping or outdoor living, removal can make the home more appealing. If the neighborhood is pool-centric, removal may reduce interest. In Los Angeles, buyer expectations vary a lot by area, lot size, and home style. A well-finished yard can help the home show better than a tired pool area, but a poor fill-in can raise concerns. Sellers should think about timing, cost, and the quality of the final landscaping. If the home will be listed soon, a clean, finished result matters more than simply making the pool disappear.
acceptedAnswer.description: Removing a pool before selling can help if buyers want more yard space or if the pool is costly to maintain and in poor condition. It can also hurt if the neighborhood strongly values pools. The best choice depends on local buyer expectations, the pool’s condition, and whether the finished yard will look complete.
